text: Many things that have been found by the archaeological excavation relate to known customs of the past. One of the skeletons from a man in his twenties had been taken from another location and reburied next to the chancel of the church at Hrísbrú. The bones of this man revealed that he had suffered from tuberculosis and died from an abscess in his brain that spread to his skull bones. A whale bone had been placed among his bones. The whale bone showed illegible carvings on one side that could have been magic runes intended to cure the man. The carving of runes on whale bones for magical purposes is known from medieval texts. For example, in Egils Saga, Egil himself saves a sick woman by finding evil runes written on a whale bone under her bed. Egil cuts down and burns the evil runes and replaces them with new runes with curative powers. By Egils interference, the woman is cured of her illness.
